heading: Quantum Computing Intelligence
subheading: Pure-plays, hedged giants & the road to commercial advantage
disclaimer: Not financial advice. This page organizes public information for research purposes only — not a recommendation to buy or sell any security. Quantum pure-plays trade at extreme valuations (P/S ~59–504×) and are highly speculative — position sizing matters more here than anywhere else on this hub. Verify current prices and do your own due diligence before investing.

kpis.label: The $300M CHIPS Act news (Sep 8) briefly lifted the pure-play trio over 10% intraday, but IonQ gave those gains back and more after its own Investor Day landed with a mixed analyst reception: IonQ fell 7.0% on the week to $36.75 (Sep 11) even as Rigetti (+0.5% to $15.27) and D-Wave (+1.3% to $16.80) held roughly flat to higher. A reminder that company-specific execution can now override even a favorable sector-wide policy catalyst

D-Wave, Rigetti and Quantinuum each finalized $100M CHIPS and Science Act R&D awards with the U.S. Department of Commerce, which is taking a minority, non-controlling equity stake in each as a condition of the grant — D-Wave already issued 7.1M shares to the government (Sep 8). PsiQuantum separately finalized its own $100M CHIPS award (Sep 8) for photonic-chip manufacturing, bringing total federal quantum CHIPS funding finalized this week to $400M

IonQ $36.75 ($14.6B mkt cap / $246.5M TTM revenue, P/S ~59×) / Rigetti $15.27 ($5.10B / $13.4M TTM, P/S ~382×) / D-Wave $16.80 ($6.26B / $12.4M TTM, P/S ~504×); Quantinuum (QNT) $49.25 (Sep 12, $12.9B mkt cap) after its own CHIPS award and an error-correction milestone; Defiance Quantum ETF (QTUM) at $147.41 (Sep 12), still well below its 52-week high of $170

tiers.label: Hedged Giants — Quantum as an Option
tiers.note: Tiered by maturity/risk — not a ranked buy list. Most quantum systems remain in R&D; true commercial systems are likely years away.

rows.angle: Smaller-scale moves after last week's blockbuster Nighthawk r2 launch: IBM Ventures led an $8M investment in BQP, an enterprise software developer, to advance its BQPhy platform for quantum-accelerated physics simulation (Sep 10); separately, IBM partnered with Lockheed Martin to open a Swiss Quantum Innovation Hub at ETH Zurich — Switzerland's first IBM Quantum Computer — tied to Swiss defense spending (Sep 10)
rows.watch for: Adoption of Nighthawk r2 (IBM Phoenix) by the pilot cohort; BQPhy commercial deployment results; Swiss Hub output; applications from IBM's own $10B quantum commercialization push

rows.angle: A fourth straight quiet week for Willow-specific hardware news; the below-threshold error-correction result stands unchallenged but unadvanced, and industry commentary continues to note Google Quantum AI's exploration of neutral-atom computing as a complement to its 105-qubit superconducting Willow chip, though no concrete new milestone landed this week
rows.watch for: Any hardware advance beyond memory preservation; output from the UK NQCC access program; specifics on the neutral-atom program; any response to IBM's Nighthawk r2 release or Quantinuum's Helix milestone

rows.angle: Its Quantinuum partnership had arguably the standout week in the whole sector: Quantinuum validated its Helix quantum-error-correction architecture on the 98-qubit Helios processor (Sep 9), posting a world-record logical memory error rate, and separately finalized its own $100M CHIPS Act award (Sep 7-8) with the U.S. government taking an equity stake
rows.watch for: Further Helix scaling results; commercial deals stemming from the Saudi Aramco MOU; Majorana milestone reproducibility on Microsoft's own topological-qubit program

rows.angle: A quieter week on NVIDIA-specific news after last week's dual demos (the IonQ/qBraid error-reduction paper and Quantinuum's Helios decoder result); NVQLink and CUDA-Q remain the connective tissue across nearly every hardware player in the sector, including this week's CHIPS Act winners
rows.watch for: Further application-native error-mitigation results; NVQLink adoption at national labs; new builder/lab additions; hybrid quantum-AI workloads

tiers.note: Tiered by maturity/risk — not a ranked buy list. Most quantum systems remain in R&D; true commercial systems are likely years away.

Riley kept $100; consensus target ~$69.25 (Strong Buy); P/S ~59×, still the cheapest of the pure-play trio

rows.angle: A genuinely active week: Rigetti finalized its own $100M CHIPS Act award (Sep 7-8) for readout-electronics miniaturization, cryogenic-capacity expansion, and high-connectivity chip-fabrication R&D, with the U.S. government taking a minority equity stake; separately, Rigetti and Purdue published a quantum-preconditioning framework showing classical Mixed-Integer Programming solvers running up to 100× faster
rows.watch for: Stock $15.27 (Sep 11, +0.5% on the week); consensus target ~$28.81 (Buy); P/S ~382×; DARPA QBI Stage B decision still pending months after Rigetti was passed over in the initial cohort

rows.watch for: Stock $16.80 (Sep 11, +1.3% on the week); consensus target ~$35.24 (Strong Buy) despite the pile-up of overhangs; TTM revenue still just $12.4M; P/S ~504×

rows.watch for: Shares continue to slide — $7.92 (Sep 11), below even last week's $8.12 low, down from the $19.11 debut-day close (Aug 28) and further beneath the original $9.79 SPAC reference price, on still no new company-specific news; first reporting quarter as a listed company still pending

private_watchlist.name: PsiQuantum
private_watchlist.note: Reportedly closed a $1.5B round (May 2026) at a ~$10.5B valuation; broke ground on its Moreton Bay Central fault-tolerant facility in Australia; partnered with Brookhaven National Laboratory (Sep 2) on fault-tolerant algorithms. New this week: finalized its own $100M CHIPS Act award with the U.S. Department of Commerce (Sep 8) to accelerate 300mm wafer production of barium titanate electro-optic material, high-temperature single-photon detectors, and automated chip-to-fiber packaging at its PsiFactory assembly facility in Milpitas, California — a separate deal from the $300M RGTI/QBTS/QNT round, structured as an R&D award rather than a public equity stake.

private_watchlist.name: Quantinuum
private_watchlist.note: Honeywell-backed; upsized $1.68B IPO raise at $60/share. A standout week: validated its Helix quantum-error-correction architecture on its 98-qubit Helios processor (Sep 9), posting a world-record logical memory error rate via a C4-Helix code that cuts spatial qubit overhead 3.5× versus traditional surface codes, with a logical Clifford error rate of 2.8×10⁻⁴ per gate (4.28× better than unencoded physical gates); and finalized its own $100M CHIPS Act award (Sep 7-8), with the government taking an equity stake, funding a GlobalFoundries 300mm wafer ion-trap fab and Monarch Quantum's laser/optics work. Shares rose to $49.25 ($12.9B mkt cap, Sep 12) on the combined news, though FY26 revenue guidance remains just $28-32M against that valuation.

private_watchlist.name: QuEra
private_watchlist.note: $230M+ raise backed by Google Quantum AI, SoftBank, NVentures; 96 verified logical qubits (Nature) — industry-leading; NVIDIA CUDA-Q/NVQLink integration partner. Outlined a gigaquop-class fault-tolerant roadmap targeting 2028-2029 (1,000+ logical qubits, 20,000+ physical qubits). No new company-specific headlines this week; reports of Google Quantum AI's own neutral-atom exploration are a competitive dynamic worth watching for QuEra's differentiation and eventual listing path.

bear_case.title: Years from commercial advantage
bear_case.description: Most systems remain R&D-phase; revenue today is mostly government contracts and research access, not commercial workloads. Even IonQ's sharply raised $450-460M FY26 guidance leans heavily on the newly acquired SkyWater foundry business, not organic quantum-services demand.

bear_case.title: A sector catalyst doesn't protect against company-specific stumbles
bear_case.description: The $300M CHIPS Act news lifted the pure-play trio over 10% intraday on Sep 8, but IonQ gave that entire move back and more the very next day after its own Investor Day drew a mixed analyst reception — ending the week down 7.0% even as Rigetti and D-Wave held roughly flat to higher. Good sector news is not a substitute for company-specific execution risk.

bear_case.title: Insiders aren't buying — and the CHIPS deals add a new form of dilution
bear_case.description: Insiders at IonQ, Rigetti and D-Wave have collectively sold a net of roughly $863M in stock over the trailing three years, with over $63M in 2026 alone and virtually no insider buying. Now the U.S. government itself holds minority equity stakes in D-Wave, Rigetti and Quantinuum as a condition of this week's $300M in CHIPS Act awards — a new class of shareholder layered on top of an already dilution-heavy funding model.

bear_case.title: Dilution as a business model
bear_case.description: Pure-plays fund R&D via repeated equity raises; share counts grow relentlessly. D-Wave alone issued 7.1M new shares to the U.S. government this week under its CHIPS award. Quantinuum's post-IPO financials still show a massive gap between $28-32M FY26 guidance and its ~$12.9B market cap, and newly listed Pasqal has now fallen to $7.92 — nearly 60% below its debut-day close in barely two weeks — a reminder that new entrants are still being priced on story, not statements.

bear_case.title: Winner may not be listed
bear_case.description: IBM/Google/Microsoft or private PsiQuantum could reach fault tolerance first, stranding pure-play premiums. PsiQuantum's own separately finalized $100M CHIPS award (Sep 8) for photonic manufacturing — on top of its Brookhaven National Lab partnership — is a fresh reminder that well-capitalized private players can out-execute rather than race the pure-plays on public markets.

catalysts.title: White House quantum executive orders enter implementation phase
catalysts.description: Federal commentary highlighted the concrete deadlines set by June's twin executive orders: a 2028 target for a scientifically-relevant quantum computer, a post-quantum cryptography migration pilot due by Dec 31, 2027, and hard PQC transition deadlines of 2030 (key establishment) and 2031 (digital signatures) for federal agencies.

catalysts.title: IBM and Lockheed Martin open Swiss Quantum Innovation Hub
catalysts.description: The hub at ETH Zurich is anchored by Switzerland's first IBM Quantum Computer and is tied to Swiss defense spending; separately, IBM Ventures led an $8M investment in BQP's BQPhy quantum-accelerated physics platform.

catalysts.title: Quantinuum validates Helix error-correction architecture
catalysts.description: On its 98-qubit Helios processor, Quantinuum posted a world-record logical memory error rate using a C4-Helix code, cutting spatial qubit overhead 3.5× versus traditional surface codes.

catalysts.title: IonQ stock falls 5.8% despite raised guidance
catalysts.description: Shares closed at $38.14 as the Investor Day failed to trigger a broad round of analyst upgrades; Mizuho cut its target to $52 while Jefferies and B. Riley raised theirs to $80 and $100 respectively.

catalysts.title: D-Wave, Rigetti and Quantinuum finalize $300M in CHIPS Act awards
catalysts.description: Each company signed a definitive $100M agreement with the U.S. Department of Commerce, with the government taking a minority, non-controlling equity stake in each; PsiQuantum separately finalized its own $100M CHIPS award for photonic manufacturing the same day.

catalysts.title: IonQ raises FY26 revenue guidance to $450-460M
catalysts.description: Announced at IonQ's Investor Day alongside the sixth-generation Superion 256 platform launch, an $8.18M Congruity360 quantum-safety deal, and a new blueprint for breaking 256-bit elliptic-curve signatures.

stance.basis: Weights are a share of a hypothetical 100% sleeve for THIS SECTOR only — not a share of your portfolio. Core and Speculative names carry the weight; Watch and Avoid deliberately carry 0% because the point of those groups is that you are not holding them yet.

positions.name: IBM
positions.note: A quieter week after last week's blockbuster Nighthawk r2 launch: an $8M IBM Ventures investment in BQP's physics-simulation platform (Sep 10) and a new Swiss Quantum Innovation Hub with Lockheed Martin at ETH Zurich (Sep 10). Trimmed a touch to fund this week's new speculative additions; still a rounding error on a profitable, dividend-paying business.

positions.name: Alphabet
positions.note: A fourth straight quiet week for Willow-specific hardware news; commentary on a potential neutral-atom pivot remains unconfirmed by any concrete milestone. Trimmed again to fund additions elsewhere; also your largest AI-sleeve holding, so size this weight with that overlap in mind.

positions.name: Microsoft
positions.note: Its Quantinuum partnership had the standout week in the sector: a world-record logical memory error rate from the validated Helix architecture (Sep 9) plus Quantinuum's own $100M CHIPS Act award (Sep 7-8). Nudged up on that combined technical and financial validation; also held in the AI sleeve — avoid double-counting.

positions.name: NVIDIA
positions.note: A quieter week on NVIDIA-specific news after last week's dual demos; NVQLink and CUDA-Q remain foundational across nearly every hardware player, including this week's CHIPS Act winners, but nothing new landed this week. Trimmed on the lack of a fresh company-specific catalyst; also your largest cross-sector AI holding, so size for that concentration too.

positions.name: IonQ
positions.note: FY26 revenue guidance nearly tripled from its prior midpoint to $450-460M at Investor Day (Sep 8), alongside the new Superion 256 platform and a fresh cybersecurity blueprint relevant to the new federal PQC deadlines. Nudged up on the scale of the guidance raise despite the stock falling 7.0% on the week on a mixed analyst reception (Mizuho cut its target; Jefferies and B. Riley raised theirs) — still the cheapest pure-play on P/S (~59×).

positions.name: Rigetti
positions.note: Two concrete catalysts in one week: its own $100M CHIPS Act award (Sep 7-8) with government equity participation, and a Purdue-partnered quantum-preconditioning framework showing up to 100× faster classical solver performance. Bumped up off the minimum on real progress; DARPA QBI Stage B decision still pending.

positions.name: Quantinuum
positions.note: New addition to the sleeve, at minimum size: the Helix world-record logical error rate (Sep 9) and its own $100M CHIPS Act award (Sep 7-8) are genuine technical and federal-backing proof points. FY26 guidance of just $28-32M against a ~$12.9B market cap is still a stark valuation gap — the reason this stays a starter position, not Core — but this week's evidence earns it small optionality exposure rather than a pure Watch. Also note the Aramco relationship overlaps with Microsoft's own AI-sleeve exposure.

positions.name: D-Wave
positions.note: Received the same $100M CHIPS Act award and government equity stake as Rigetti and Quantinuum this week — a genuine federal vote of confidence — but that doesn't resolve what kept this in Avoid last week: the Q2 revenue miss, the CFO transition, and a securities-litigation investigation that has widened to four law firms remain unresolved. Federal funding is a tailwind, not an answer to those open questions.

positions.name: Pasqal
positions.note: Continues to slide: shares closed at $7.92 (Sep 11), below even last week's $8.12 low and now further beneath the original $9.79 SPAC reference price, on still no new company-specific news. A stock that's lost over half its debut-day value in barely two weeks with zero independent public financials is an Avoid, not a Watch.
